items.title: R-meta-3022-1
items.body:
Reduces `L-meta-3022` (Petersen minus a vertex, first gate `x_0 || x_2`, second gate `OR(pins)`, remaining `≤ 13` gates) into 5 clean subgoals:
1. `no14`: collapses all 49 redundant `pins` cases (length ≤ 1, out-of-range wire 10, duplicate pins, or both pins in `{0, 2, 9}`) by rewiring wire 10 away into a 14-gate circuit for `Petersen - v`.
2. `no14_del4`: collapses all 48 cases touching a degree-2 vertex `{4, 6, 7}` via explicit automorphisms of `Petersen - v` mapping `v ↦ 4` and pinning `x_4 = false` (eliminating the second OR gate) into a 14-gate circuit for `(Petersen - v) - 4`.
3. `many_nots`: strips all circuits with `notCount ≥ 3` via `13 ≤ C.size - PEqualNP.NotBracket.notCount C`.
4. `core_no9`: symmetry-reduces the remaining 28 non-wire-9 pairs under the involution `(0 2)(3 5)(4 7)` (which fixes `x_0 || x_2`) and OR commutativity to 8 canonical pairs with `notCount ≤ 2`.
5. `core_with9`: symmetry-reduces the remaining 8 wire-9 pairs to 3 canonical 3-way ORs (`k ∈ {1, 3, 8}`) with `notCount ≤ 2`.

Verified locally: `lake build PEqualNP.Outside.R_meta_3022_1` (5.0s, 0 errors, 0 warnings), `import PEqualNP.Defs` only, `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` axioms, 0 extra module constants, structural conclusion match.

items.title: L-meta-3911: reduce thirteen gate pairs by Petersen graph symmetry
items.body:
The thirteen allowed second-gate input pairs fall into six classes under symmetries of the nine-vertex graph. Both prescribed gates read only primary inputs, so commuting them puts the AND gate first. The proof renames all later wires, preserves their values (including out-of-range reads), and adds exactly two gates. A residual circuit of size at most thirteen would therefore contradict the sixteen-gate lower bound for its class.

The four hypotheses correspond to the six existing first-AND bounds in L-meta-1667 through L-meta-1672. The first hypothesis groups the cases (0,1), (0,2), and (0,3). The other three cover (0,4), (0,6), and (4,6). The desk lists only PEqualNP.Defs as a project import for L-meta-3911.

items.title: L-meta-3225: exclude a fourteen-gate circuit satisfying both Petersen cofactors
items.body:
The proof declares inductive types and a structure for the finite circuit certificate and needs a reader under the plain-file rules.

Suppose the same tail computes both specified cofactors. Given an arbitrary nine-bit input x, feed the eight-variable circuit description the coordinates (x1, x0, x5, x8, x2, x4, x7, x3) and set its control to x6. Its first nine input wires are then exactly x, and wire 9 is x0 OR x6. At x6 = false the ten-edge target is the induced eight-vertex graph. At x6 = true the target also accepts x1 or x8, the two neighbors of vertex 6. Thus the tail would compute the full nine-vertex edge function with OR(x0,x6) supplied in at most 14 gates. This argument also gives the exclusion without the two hypotheses about readers.

The lower bound for that input bank uses zakpgrove's live-set and rank certificate from #10495, pinned at 8397d94eefc6d8e9aef2a184fe946911f2104d1b. Its antecedents include MohammadESteitieh's #5821 and PressF10's #4332. The cofactor reconstruction and its application to the exact L-meta-3225 statement are provided here.

The rank check handles one label by testing whether any constraint requires distinct labels. For two labels and at most twelve wires, each bit of a 4,096-bit table represents one labeling. Every valid labeling survives the intersection of the constraint tables. These two cases account for 2,975 rank tests in the supplied certificate.

When the state retains all nine raw inputs, the low nine frontier bits give a candidate original input. When exactly one raw input is missing, the proof inserts each value of that bit into the retained coordinates. The checker tests the actual graph output and every remaining wire before using either candidate. The original force check handles other cases and failed candidates. Across distinct output requirements within each eligible state, the direct test supplies 47,023 of 54,110 witnesses with all inputs retained and 32,093 of 35,135 with one missing. Smaller blocks allow the kernel to replay the search in parts.

items.title: L-meta-3971: reduce the Petersen bound to circuits that reuse gates
items.body:
L-meta-3971 asks whether a 14-gate circuit with a single NOT gate and restricted access to one input can compute a specified Petersen graph function on all 512 assignments.

The reduction unfolds the output into a tree and counts its leaves and inverter occurrences. The first child states that a tree with at most one inverter and at most 14 gates disagrees with the target somewhere. The second child keeps the original circuit restrictions and asks the same question for outputs with larger unfoldings or repeated inverter occurrences.

I checked the first child separately in Lean. The proof uses signed rectangle bounds and checks 19,466 possible sampled truth columns for the expression feeding the inverter. The second child, which permits a gate output to be reused, remains open.

[Lean sources and independent build instructions for the first child](https://github.com/Simlowker/pequalnp-proofs/tree/bfe00e79348840acf0a6753d2afc4026a8255b93/certificates/L-meta-3971).

A further [integer certificate](https://github.com/Simlowker/pequalnp-proofs/tree/bfe00e79348840acf0a6753d2afc4026a8255b93/certificates/L-meta-3971/shared-inverter) checks the case where the inverter may have arbitrary fan-out and each binary gate is used at most once in the live circuit. Any 14-gate counterexample must therefore reuse an AND or OR gate. This extension was verified with the supplied Python program.

items.title: L-meta-3616: reduce the Petersen circuit bound to distinct truth columns
items.body:
L-meta-3616 asks whether 14 two-input AND/OR gates can realize the 29 labeled Petersen inputs when the negation of input zero is also available.

The reduction stores each wire as a 29-bit truth column and an unfolded leaf count. It skips a gate whenever an earlier wire already has its truth column. Commutativity lets each surviving gate use its operands in increasing index order.

The first child asks for an invariant proving that the target column requires at least 17 unfolded leaves. I verified this child separately in Lean using a signed rectangle certificate on the 16 positive and 13 negative rows. A 16-gate formula attains the bound. The second child is the remaining finite search over at most 14 gates with distinct truth columns and at least 17 leaves at the output. That circuit lower bound remains open.

items.title: Bound the wire indices in L-meta-4850
items.body: The reduction bounds the wire indices in the Petersen circuit search. A legal read keeps its index, and a read of an unavailable wire uses a single reserved index that always reads false. The normalization also makes every gate have two input positions while preserving size and evaluation.

items.title: L-meta-4277
items.body: Direct proof using the merged two-vertex lower-bound certificate from L-meta-2442. Prepend NOT of input 0 to the alleged 14-gate circuit. This gives a legal 15-gate circuit whose first gate computes the complemented bit and whose output would compute the Petersen-minus-a-vertex edge function, contradicting that certificate. The probe's pair-list encoding is checked against the original function.

items.title: L-meta-4608
items.body:
This file defines inductive types and structures used by the finite Petersen circuit certificate. It proves the posted L-meta-4608 statement by prepending the two permitted OR gates and applying the sixteen-gate lower bound. The specialization follows NoGod3524's proof of L-meta-3590 (#7511).

This revision uses copsrlpond's certificate from L-meta-2834 (#6962), which builds on the work of JLDC (#6373) and PressF10 (L-meta-1667). Its only project import is `PEqualNP.Defs`. The project checker run locally accepted this revision against the exact posted statement.

items.title: L-meta-2159: split off the NOT-free size-15 case
items.body:
Reduction of L-meta-2159 into two children.

- `h1` is verbatim the statement of `PEqualNP.Outside.L_meta_2331`, which this library already proves: `FanInTwo C` and `circuitFun 9 C = <the Petersen-minus-vertex function>` give `15 ≤ C.size`.
- `h2` is the case that neither `L_meta_2331` nor the three-NOT sibling `L_meta_2165` covers: the same function with every gate AND or OR (no NOT) at size exactly 15, refuted.

The glue is three lines: `intro` the hypotheses, apply `h1` for the lower bound, apply `h2` for the inequality, close with `omega`.

items.title: L-meta-1886: Prove relabeling and wire-10 cut internally
items.body: Reduces L-meta-1886 by proving internally both the input-relabeling normalization and the constant-propagation cut eliminating wire 10, leaving 3 clean independent subgoals: (1) noExtraWire: plain 10-input FanInTwo circuit of size <= 18 computing Petersen f10 (when wire 10 is unused); (2) firstAnd_residual: plain 10-input FanInTwo circuit of size <= 17 matching f10 on (x 0 && x 1) = false (when wire 10 is used and b = true); (3) firstOr_used: size <= 18 circuit with wire 10 = (x 0 || x 1) genuinely read by at least one gate. Verified with lake env lean (LEAN_EXIT=0) and outside-guard.mjs reduce (GUARD_EXIT=0).

items.title: R-meta-4310-1
items.body:
Reduction of `L-meta-4310` (Petersen graph minus a vertex, first gate OR(x_0, x_6): fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuits computing its edge function need at least 15 gates) to four statements, one per shape of the second gate.

The elimination is proved in the file: with fewer than 15 gates, at least 13 of them AND/OR and at most one NOT, the second gate exists, and by its operation and its input wires it falls into exactly one of the four children.

1. second gate is NOT (any input)
2. second gate is AND/OR reading at most one wire
3. second gate is AND/OR reading two existing wires (both < 11)
4. second gate is AND/OR reading a wire that does not exist yet (some input >= 11)

**Checks run.** The module builds (`lake build PEqualNP.Outside.R_meta_4310_1`), and the project verifier (`tools/check-lean.mjs`, kind `reduce`) accepted it locally: ACCEPTED (reduce), 4 children, axioms [propext, Quot.sound] only.

items.title: L-meta-3225 (reduction): exclude all 36 raw pair conjunctions
items.body:
A fourteen-gate tail satisfying both cofactors would give a fifteen-gate circuit for the Petersen graph with one vertex removed. This reduction proves that none of its tail wires can equal the AND of any two distinct raw inputs on all 512 rows.

If a gate at any position computes such a conjunction, replace it by a first gate on those two inputs. The proof permutes the wire indices, preserves unavailable-wire reads, and proves the resulting circuit has the same size, fan-in, and truth table. Twelve graph symmetries carry the 36 unordered input pairs to the six first-AND cases already checked as L-meta-1667 through L-meta-1672. The first child packages those six cases. The second child is the remaining fourteen-gate obstruction after excluding all 36 conjunctions at every gate.

For the normalized search that discards constant and repeated full truth columns and tracks use of raw control wire 6, the restriction reduces the possible first columns from 86 to 58 and the distinct two-gate traces from 8,595 to 4,157. The remaining finite search is open.

items.title: R-meta-4643-73: isolate ordinary errors using the NOT budget and first-gate bounds
items.body:
This reduction tests the circuit on its ordinary ten inputs. A wrong output survives the mask whenever the pivot already has the mask polarity, or the companion wire has the neutral value. The two remaining error searches use this criterion.

The first child is L-meta-4308, which already has an authoritative ACCEPTED verdict. Inserting the mask after the companion adds one binary gate and preserves the NOT count. The binary-gate bound therefore leaves at most one NOT in the original 13 gates. [L-meta-4308](https://github.com/open-goat/pequalnp-proofs/pull/10164#issuecomment-7146873337)

The second child excludes a first companion that computes an AND of two distinct original inputs. I checked this child separately in Lean using TheWaler’s merged L-meta-3275. Put the raw AND first, put the supplied OR second, and exchange their wire numbers in the tail. The twelve Petersen automorphisms route every raw pair to one of the six certified representatives. [L-meta-3275](https://github.com/open-goat/pequalnp-proofs/pull/6547)

The third child allows at most one NOT and places none before or at the companion. In the fourth child the unique NOT is in that prefix. The suffix is then monotone, which forces every ordinary error of a successful masked circuit to have the same target label as the mask polarity. The local warehouse verifier accepted all four children and replayed 1,682 constants.

I also replayed the 29 certificate blocks of Julleht’s direct proof in separate Lean modules and checked their assembly. Applying the resulting seeded lower bound closes the last two children locally. I then applied all four proofs to this reduction and checked the exact desk statement. The mask insertion follows the wiring argument for L-meta-3614. [Merged wiring proof](https://github.com/open-goat/pequalnp-proofs/pull/7428) · [Direct proof and original certificate attribution](https://github.com/open-goat/pequalnp-proofs/pull/9415)

items.title: Reduce L-meta-5054 by counting distinct row and column profiles
items.body:
For L-meta-5054, divide the nine input variables into two groups. Holding the first group fixed gives a row of the edge-function truth table, and holding the second fixed gives a column. If each of the six observed wires depends on just one group, a collision-free six-bit signature must distinguish every combination of a distinct row and a distinct column. There are at most 64 signatures.

The first child proves the counting implication for any Boolean function and six observations. The proof chooses one representative of each row and column. Two equal signatures on representative pairs would give equal function values after varying either group, forcing both representatives to denote the same profiles. The second child retains only circuits satisfying this bound on every split where the wires separate.

For the split {0,4,6,7} and its complement, the Petersen-minus-a-vertex edge function gives 12 distinct rows and 12 distinct columns. A 12-by-12 witness matrix and the contradiction with six separated wires both compiled independently in Lean. A separate exhaustive enumeration found a product above 64 on 102 of the 126 four-versus-five splits. A collision-free cut must have at least one wire depending on both groups for every one of these 102 splits. The remaining circuit argument is open.

The project checker accepted the exact reduction and the source guard passed. The following standalone Lean file compiled against the exact first-child type.

<details>
<summary>Lean proof of the first child</summary>

~~~lean
import Mathlib
import PEqualNP.Defs
namespace Profile5054

theorem collision {A B I : Type} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [Fintype I]
    (f : A → B → Bool) (s : A → B → I → Bool)
    (pure : ∀ k, (∀ a b b', s a b k = s a b' k) ∨ (∀ a a' b, s a b k = s a' b k))
    (small : 2^(Fintype.card I) < (Set.range f).ncard * (Set.range (fun b a => f a b)).ncard) :
    ∃ a b a' b', f a b ≠ f a' b' ∧ s a b = s a' b' := by
  classical
  by_contra no
  have decode {a b a' b'} (h : s a b = s a' b') : f a b = f a' b' := by
    by_contra neq
    exact no ⟨a,b,a',b',neq,h⟩
  let encode (q : Set.range f × Set.range (fun b a => f a b)) := s q.1.property.choose q.2.property.choose
  have inj : Function.Injective encode := by
    intro l r h
    let a := l.1.property.choose
    let b := l.2.property.choose
    let c := r.1.property.choose
    let d := r.2.property.choose
    have eq (i : I) : s a b i = s c d i := congrFun h i
    apply Prod.ext
    · apply Subtype.ext
      rw [← l.1.property.choose_spec, ← r.1.property.choose_spec]
      funext y
      apply decode
      funext i
      rcases pure i with h|h
      · exact (h a y b).trans ((eq i).trans (h c d y))
      · exact h a c y
    · apply Subtype.ext
      rw [← l.2.property.choose_spec, ← r.2.property.choose_spec]
      funext x
      apply decode
      funext i
      rcases pure i with h|h
      · exact h x b d
      · exact (h x a b).trans ((eq i).trans (h c x d))
  have le := Fintype.card_le_of_injective _ inj
  rw [Fintype.card_prod,Fintype.card_fun,Fintype.card_bool] at le
  apply (not_lt_of_ge le)
  simpa only [Set.fintypeCard_eq_ncard] using small

end Profile5054


namespace Cut5054

theorem split {n : Nat} (f : (Fin n → Bool) → Bool) (S : Finset Nat)
    (observe : (Fin n → Bool) → Nat → Bool) (six : S.card = 6)
    (m : Set (Fin n)) [DecidablePred (· ∈ m)]
    (pure : ∀ w ∈ S, DependsOn (fun x => observe x w) m ∨
                     DependsOn (fun x => observe x w) mᶜ)
    (large : let M := fun (a b : Fin n → Bool) => f (fun i => if i ∈ m then a i else b i)
             64 < (Set.range M).ncard * (Set.range (fun b a => M a b)).ncard) :
    ∃ x y, f x ≠ f y ∧ ∀ w ∈ S, observe x w = observe y w := by
  let merge (a b : Fin n → Bool) (i : Fin n) := if i ∈ m then a i else b i
  let M a b := f (merge a b)
  let sig a b (k : ↥S) := observe (merge a b) k
  have sep (k : ↥S) : (∀ a b d, sig a b k = sig a d k) ∨
      (∀ a c b, sig a b k = sig c b k) := by
    rcases pure k k.property with l|r
    · left; intro a b d; apply l; intro i hi; simp [merge,hi]
    · right; intro a c b; apply r; intro i hi
      have hn : i ∉ m := hi
      simp [merge,hn]
  have cap : 2 ^ Fintype.card (↥S) < (Set.range M).ncard * (Set.range (fun b a => M a b)).ncard := by
    simpa [Fintype.card_coe,six,M,merge] using large
  obtain ⟨a,b,c,d,neq,eq⟩ := Profile5054.collision M sig sep cap
  exact ⟨merge a b,merge c d,neq,fun w hw => congrFun eq ⟨w,hw⟩⟩
end Cut5054

example : ∀ (f : (Fin 9 → Bool) → Bool) (S : Finset Nat) (obs : (Fin 9 → Bool) → Nat → Bool),
      S.card = 6 → ∀ m : Finset (Fin 9), let M := fun (a b : Fin 9 → Bool) => f (fun i => if i ∈ m then a i else b i);
      (∀ w ∈ S, DependsOn (fun x => obs x w) (m : Set (Fin 9)) ∨ DependsOn (fun x => obs x w) (m : Set (Fin 9))ᶜ) → 64 < (Set.range M).ncard * (Set.range (fun b a => M a b)).ncard →
      ∃ x y, f x ≠ f y ∧ ∀ w ∈ S, obs x w = obs y w := fun f S obs six m pure cap => Cut5054.split f S obs six (m : Set (Fin 9)) pure cap

~~~
</details>
